findings.message: The two arrows use different scales. The step arrow is drawn at 2× the step length and the slope arrow at 0.2× the gradient. This only looks consistent at learning rate 0.1. At any other rate the two lengths can't be compared. Draw both arrows on one stated scale, either both as gradient-sized vectors or both as displacements, and name that one scale in the assumptions.
The arrow labelled 'Step taken' shows the next step, which hasn't happened yet. The description itself says 'next step'. Rename the label to 'Next step'.

The Status readout (running / paused / diverged / converged) doesn't appear in the readout line. Without it, the promised 'diverged' outcome isn't shown. Divergence wasn't sampled in these captures (stretch 4 never diverges at rates up to 0.3).

The ball can only be dragged along x. The plan promises dragging 'on the surface' to choose any starting point. The assumptions disclose the x-only drag, but you can't pick a new start across the valley.

The arrows use mixed scales: the step arrow is 2× the step and the slope arrow is 0.2× the gradient. At learning rate 0.05 the step arrow shows a misleading half of the slope arrow, because of the scale choice rather than the step itself. Use one disclosed scale for both arrows.

Near the bottom, both arrows shrink to stubs that are mostly hidden by the ball (radius 0.16). The labels 'Slope (uphill)' and 'Step taken' then float near the ball, and 'Slope (uphill)' sits on top of the orange trail. The learner can't see the slope or the step. Scale the arrows so they stay visibly longer than the ball, or shrink the ball, and keep the labels off the trail.
The arrows use mixed scales: at learning rate 0.3 the step arrow is drawn at 0.6× the gradient but the slope arrow at 0.2×. Use one disclosed scale for both arrows.

The arrows are tiny and covered by the ball. 'Slope (uphill)' points at an arrow you can't see, and 'Step taken' sits over the trail. The zig-zag across the steep direction at rate 0.3 is barely readable, because the trail draws only one point every 4 steps and turns into long straight segments.
Divergence isn't reachable at the default stretch of 4 (0.3 × 4 = 1.2 < 2), and no capture sampled stretch at 7 or above with a high rate. So the promised 'flies off' behaviour wasn't checked.
Same arrow-scale mismatch as in the default view (step arrow at 2×, slope arrow at 0.2×).
The arrows use mixed scales (step arrow at 2×, slope arrow at 0.2×).
From this angle too, the arrows are hidden under the ball and only the labels show, crowded around it.
The arrows use mixed scales (step arrow at 2×, slope arrow at 0.2×).
The slope arrow can't be seen under the ball, and the 'Step taken' label overlaps the trail.
The 'Status' readout (running/paused/diverged/converged) does not appear in the readout line of any capture. The plan's assumptions only list step, loss and distance. Divergence was not sampled.
Dragging is limited to the flat (x) direction, where the plan says 'drag the ball on the surface'. This is disclosed in the assumptions.

The trail only marks every 4th step (step%4). Across the steep direction the ball flips sides every step, so an even sampling interval always lands on the same side and the zig-zag is never drawn. The plan promises the path 'zig-zags across the steep direction' and 'bounces between the steep walls'; with this sampling, stretch 10 at a rate near 0.15 would look smooth. Use an odd interval, or draw every step for a recent window.

The 'Next step ÷ rate' label box is about five times longer than the short step arrow it names. The label hide threshold (arrow length > 0.25) is too low; raise it so the label shows only when the arrow is clearly longer.

At learning rate 0.3 the across-valley step flips sign every step, yet the trail is a smooth curve. It marks every 4th step, an even interval, which hides the period-2 bounce the plan promises. The divergence and stretch-10 cases were not sampled.
Same problem: sampling every 4th step aliases away the zig-zag across the steep direction.
The 'Next step ÷ rate' label is much larger than the tiny step arrow it names.
The trail drawn at the high learning rate hides the step-to-step oscillation because of the even 4-step sampling.
